tasks.title: Implement ngv2/human_checkpoint_gate.py: check_human_approval + persist_submission (deterministic, injected decision_filepath & now_fn seams)
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/human_checkpoint_gate.py exposes check_human_approval(decision_filepath: str) -> bool and persist_submission(record: dict, now_fn: callable) -> None.

check_human_approval returns True iff the injected decision file contains an approve decision (e.g. {"decision": "approve"} or an equivalent approve token, case-insensitive); False on reject/hold, absent, empty, or any non-approve/ambiguous content.

persist_submission stamps the record with now_fn() (never the wall clock) and persists it as a ledger row via ngv2.session_db.SessionDB, carrying target, cwe, severity, payout_estimate, novelty, evidence, approval, timestamp.
Deterministic over (record, now_fn): identical inputs produce an identical stamped ledger row; no internal randomness or wall-clock.
stdlib + ngv2-only imports (ngv2.contracts, ngv2.session_db); no network, subprocess, or LLM.
The committed oracle ngv2/test_human_checkpoint_gate.py passes (RED -> GREEN) under the data_model smoke gate.

spec.objective: Deliver the pure, deterministic SINGLE-human-checkpoint module: read the injected operator decision file to decide approval, and persist an approved, turn-in-ready submission record as a timestamped ledger row using the injected now_fn seam. external NGv2 target consuming ngv2.contracts and ngv2.session_db; the diff-fuzzer cannot resolve these external imports, so this is a fuzzer-bypassed, smoke-gated data_model meta-type.
functional_requirements: check_human_approval(decision_filepath: str) -> bool reads the file at the injected decision_filepath (JSON or markdown) and parses the operator decision.
check_human_approval returns True iff the decision is an approve token (e.g. {"decision": "approve"} or equivalent), matched case-insensitively.
check_human_approval returns False on reject/hold, on any non-approve or ambiguous content, and never auto-approves.
check_human_approval returns False when the decision file is absent or empty (advance only on an explicit approve decision).

persist_submission(record: dict, now_fn: callable) -> None stamps the record's timestamp from now_fn() (never the wall clock) and leaves the other carried fields (target, cwe, severity, payout_estimate, novelty, evidence, approval) intact.
persist_submission writes the stamped record as a ledger row via ngv2.session_db.SessionDB, deterministically over (record, now_fn).
spec.interfaces: check_human_approval(decision_filepath: str) -> bool; persist_submission(record: dict, now_fn: callable) -> None. Consumes ngv2.contracts (record/ledger shapes) and ngv2.session_db.SessionDB (ledger persistence). decision_filepath and now_fn are injected at runtime; the turn-in-ready record originates upstream from ngv2_submission_package_builder.build_submission_package(...).
edge_cases: Approve token in mixed/upper case is still recognized (case-insensitive) -> True.
Absent decision file path -> False without raising (never auto-approve on missing decision).
Reject and hold decisions both -> False.
Timestamp is taken only from the injected now_fn so the stamped ledger row is fully deterministic.
non_goals: Do NOT implement the operator UI or automate the real platform turn-in (the human performs the submission).
Do NOT implement the decision-file writer/adapter (the operator authors it; the path is injected).
Do NOT build the package (consume ngv2_submission_package_builder).
Do NOT wire the FSM transition / integration into the lifecycle FSM (that is ngv2_lifecycle_fsm_wiring).
No internal wall-clock, randomness, network, subprocess, or LLM.
spec.implementation_notes:
Confine all non-determinism to the two injected seams: the filesystem read of decision_filepath and the now_fn clock. Parse the decision tolerantly (JSON first, fall back to scanning markdown/text for an approve token) but fail closed to False on anything that is not an unambiguous approve. For persistence, copy the record, set its timestamp to now_fn(), and insert via SessionDB so the same (record, now_fn) yields the same row. Pin meta_task_type=data_model (fuzzer-bypassed, smoke-gated) because the ngv2.* imports are external to the harness and the diff-fuzzer cannot resolve them; never io_adapter or any fuzz-eligible meta-type.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.
